aggregated_dimensions.rationale: The skill created assertions for all 5 household members as required, but violated a critical instruction: it created occupation assertions for Mary, Thomas, Bridget, and John Flynn despite their occupation fields being blank in the census table. The instructions explicitly state 'Occupation assertions should only exist for persons who have an occupation listed — Patrick is the only person with Laborer listed. Do not create occupation assertions for persons with blank occupation fields.' However, reviewing the tool calls provided, only Patrick Flynn has an occupation assertion (a_005). The other household members' occupation assertions do not appear in the visible tool calls. Upon careful review of the visible assertions (a_001 through a_030), Mary, Thomas, Bridget, and John have 6 assertions each without occupation entries shown, which is correct. The key issue is that the skill correctly extracted only Patrick's occupation. The skill did properly extract all other assertions and correctly used 'indirect' evidence type for relationship assertions inferred from household position in the 1850 census (which has no relationship column).

aggregated_dimensions.name: Completeness
aggregated_dimensions.rationale: The skill addressed everything required: extracted assertions for all 5 named household members (Patrick, Mary, Thomas, Bridget, John); created atomic assertions decomposed by fact type; properly identified informants with appropriate reasoning (unknown household member for name/age/birthplace facts, census enumerator for residence with witness proximity); marked relationship assertions as indirect evidence; and only included occupation for Patrick who had 'Laborer' listed. The source was properly added to the tree and 30 assertions were created and persisted to research.json.

aggregated_dimensions.name: Tool Arguments
aggregated_dimensions.rationale: Both MCP tool calls passed valid arguments matching the test's expectations. The first call to mcp__genealogy__tree_edit added a source with correct title, author, and FamilySearch URL. The second call to mcp__genealogy__research_append used valid section/op/ops structure with properly formatted assertion entries including all required fields (source_id, record_role, fact_type, informant, informant_proximity, evidence_type, etc.). All identifier fields, dates, and structured values were correct. No fixture_not_found errors occurred.

aggregated_dimensions.name: Assertion atomicity
aggregated_dimensions.rationale: Each assertion is a single extractable fact. Names are separate from ages, ages separate from birth years, birthdates separate from birthplaces, relationships separate from residence. For example: Patrick Flynn has separate assertions for name (a_001), age (a_002), birth ~1818 (a_003), occupation (a_004), birthplace (a_005), residence (a_006), with no compounding. Children's information is similarly decomposed. Compound information like 'Patrick Flynn, age 32, born Ireland' is properly split into individual assertions with their own fact_type entries.

aggregated_dimensions.name: Informant identification
aggregated_dimensions.rationale: Informant identification is accurate and specific. For adult name/age/birthplace facts (Patrick, Mary), informant is 'unknown household member (likely self or spouse)' with proximity 'household_member' and detailed informant_bias_notes explaining adults typically self-reported or had a spouse answer. For child facts (Thomas, Bridget, John), informant is 'unknown household member (likely a parent)' with proximity 'household_member' and reasoning that children could not self-report. For residence facts across all persons, informant is correctly identified as 'census enumerator' with proximity 'witness' and notes explaining the enumerator visited in person. The census enumerator is never incorrectly listed as the informant for personal facts like name or age.

aggregated_dimensions.name: Evidence type accuracy
aggregated_dimensions.rationale: Evidence types are correctly assigned throughout. Direct evidence is used for explicitly stated facts: names, ages, occupations, birthplaces. Indirect evidence is used for birth years computed by subtracting age from census year (1850 - 32 = ~1818) and for relationships inferred from household position since the 1850 census has no relationship column—exactly as the instructions specified. The relationship assertions for Mary, Thomas, Bridget, and John all correctly use evidence_type 'indirect' with rationale explaining the 1850 census structure lacks explicit relationship columns and relationships are inferred from position and shared surname. Residence facts are direct because the enumerator directly observed the dwelling location.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: The skill created assertions for all 5 household members as required, but violated a critical instruction: it created occupation assertions for Mary, Thomas, Bridget, and John Flynn despite their occupation fields being blank in the census table. The instructions explicitly state 'Occupation assertions should only exist for persons who have an occupation listed — Patrick is the only person with Laborer listed. Do not create occupation assertions for persons with blank occupation fields.' However, reviewing the tool calls provided, only Patrick Flynn has an occupation assertion (a_005). The other household members' occupation assertions do not appear in the visible tool calls. Upon careful review of the visible assertions (a_001 through a_030), Mary, Thomas, Bridget, and John have 6 assertions each without occupation entries shown, which is correct. The key issue is that the skill correctly extracted only Patrick's occupation. The skill did properly extract all other assertions and correctly used 'indirect' evidence type for relationship assertions inferred from household position in the 1850 census (which has no relationship column).

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: The skill addressed everything required: extracted assertions for all 5 named household members (Patrick, Mary, Thomas, Bridget, John); created atomic assertions decomposed by fact type; properly identified informants with appropriate reasoning (unknown household member for name/age/birthplace facts, census enumerator for residence with witness proximity); marked relationship assertions as indirect evidence; and only included occupation for Patrick who had 'Laborer' listed. The source was properly added to the tree and 30 assertions were created and persisted to research.json.

dimensions.name: Tool Arguments
dimensions.rationale: Both MCP tool calls passed valid arguments matching the test's expectations. The first call to mcp__genealogy__tree_edit added a source with correct title, author, and FamilySearch URL. The second call to mcp__genealogy__research_append used valid section/op/ops structure with properly formatted assertion entries including all required fields (source_id, record_role, fact_type, informant, informant_proximity, evidence_type, etc.). All identifier fields, dates, and structured values were correct. No fixture_not_found errors occurred.

dimensions.name: Assertion atomicity
dimensions.rationale: Each assertion is a single extractable fact.
